submitted.rationale: Of the 3 measured compositions, only the Fe-rich one (Fe0.62 Ni0.22 V0.16) gave a positive photocurrent, 1.5e-7 A under 2.4 eV light. This fits a hematite-like absorber with a gap near 2.1 eV.

rejected.reason: Close to FeVO4 stoichiometry. MACE puts FeVO4 on the hull, but this composition measured 0 A.
V-rich corner. It measured -1e-8 A, which is effectively zero.

consultations.verdict: Weakly supportive/largely uninformative: MEGNet HSE gap 2.75 eV for mp-504509 (queried as a Fe-V-O reference). Index 99 (Fe0.41Ni0.18V0.41) sits near FeVO4 stoichiometry, a known visible-absorbing photoanode (~2.0-2.1 eV exp. gap) which can absorb 2.4 eV photons; Ni fraction is near the library minimum. Measure.

FeVO4 (mp-504509) is on the hull (MACE), yet the FeVO4-like composition idx 99 gave 0 photocurrent, so the stable vanadate alone doesn't explain activity. Against more of the Fe:V~1 region. Switch to the Fe-rich corner (idx 83, Fe0.62), where hematite-like Fe2O3 (gap ~2.1 eV) can absorb 2.4 eV light. Treat the model result as uninformative about this candidate. Measure it to explore.

Uninformative for this candidate. MEGNet PBE gives 2.08 eV for FeVO4, but that composition measured zero, so the band gap alone does not predict activity here. I already have a nonzero Fe-rich result (idx 83), so I'll spend the last measurement on the densely sampled, still-unexplored V-rich region. Idx 3 (V0.68, Fe0.15, Ni0.17) is V2O5-like, with a gap near 2.3 eV that can absorb 2.4 eV light.
